dedupe_keys.name: world bank private participation in infrastructure ppi project database

description: The PPI Project Database records contractual arrangements for public infrastructure projects in low- and middle-income countries that have reached financial closure and in which private parties take on operating risk, with country coverage across six regions. It covers electricity generation, transmission and distribution, natural gas transmission and distribution, ICT backbone including cables, airports, railways, toll roads, bridges and tunnels, ports, potable water, sewerage and integrated municipal solid waste. Projects qualify with at least 20 percent private participation (5 percent equity for divestitures) and must serve the public; investment is recorded as total commitments in millions of US dollars in the year of financial closure, including the public share, and cancelled projects are kept. Information comes only from public sources. The World Bank publishes annual and half-year global reports, and 2024 commitments reached 100.7 billion dollars. The database is accessible online through country, sector and region snapshots and a custom query, with free downloads to Excel, Word or HTML and a simplified Microsoft Access file. Caveats: public investment and high-income countries are excluded, figures are nominal commitments, not spending, and reliance on public sources carries a risk of inaccuracy. It supports economic and investment appraisal of infrastructure across sectors and, with asset data, exposure studies of privately operated assets; a related record is the Global Infrastructure Resilience Index (GIRI).
